children: CIF basis bids and offers for soybeans loaded on barges and delivered to U.S. Gulf Coast export terminals were mostly steady to higher and corn bids were mixed on Thursday as futures headed down and low water levels slowed barge traffic, according to market players.
CIF bids for soybeans rose by 4 cents for barges loaded in September, 13 cents for those loaded in October and 2 cents for barges loaded in December.
CIF bids for corn fell by 2 cents for barges loaded in September, and 1 cent for barges loaded in October, November and December. They rose by 1 cent for January, February and March.

CIF values for soybeans and corn received support as lower water levels on the Mississippi River are causing shippers to move lighter loads, resulting in fewer crops being transported through Gulf export terminals, according to a dealer.
FOB corn offers were down 1 cent for barges loaded in the first half of October.
They were down 3 cents each for barges loaded in the last half of October, November and December.
Exporters sold 192,000 metric tons of soybeans to China for 2026/2027 delivery, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture said new-crop U.S. corn export sales in the week ended August 27 are at 1,986,400 metric tons, above trade estimates for 500,000 to 1,600,000 tons. The agency also reported net cancellations of 829,600 tons of old-crop sales.

The USDA said new-crop U.S. soybean export sales in the week ended August 27 are at 1,948,400 metric tons, in line with trade estimates for 1,400,000 to 2,500,000 tons. The agency also reported net cancellations of 94,200 tons of old-crop sales.
